fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestShipHeadBuildOnDemand shows, with SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA naming a missing binary and SHIP_HEAD_BUILD set, ship's render and ship close-out running SHIP_HEAD_BUILD once in the worktree and then rendering with the built binary; with SHIP_HEAD_BUILD empty, the missing binary failing with its 'not a built rhiza' error; and a failing SHIP_HEAD_BUILD failing with nothing rendered or pushed. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/ship-land-branch-build passes, with a new case where SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA is missing and SHIP_HEAD_BUILD is set and ship land builds it, logs to head.log and lands. Touches internal/api/ship_build.go, internal/api/ship_build_test.go and cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/ship-land-branch-build.txtar.
fields.statement: When the run's workflow sets SHIP_HEAD_BUILD and the SHIP_HEAD_RHIZA binary it names does not exist yet, the ship commands that land or render with it (ship land, ship close-out and every ship render) run SHIP_HEAD_BUILD themselves (sh -c, in the worktree) and then use the built binary, as ship rebase already does, so a workflow with no head-build steps (Rhiza's ship-rhiza over the conductor default) renders and closes out with the branch's own rhiza. With SHIP_HEAD_BUILD empty, a missing binary still fails with nothing landed, rendered or pushed, and a failed build fails the same way, carrying the build's output.
